claims.claim_vi: Python tutorial: class variables are shared by all instances, instance variables are unique; derived classes resolve attributes up the base chain; all methods are effectively virtual (overridable); 'private' instance variables that cannot be accessed except from inside an object do not exist, a leading underscore is a convention, and a double-underscore name is mangled to _classname__name.
claims.section: Class and Instance Variables; Inheritance; Private Variables
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of python/cpython at commit 7dbc7975db8e34db8be8e4a10bd10784ab49b07a.

claims.claim_vi: Glossary: duck-typing looks at the interface rather than the type and allows polymorphic substitution; abstract base classes complement duck-typing by defining interfaces and cannot be instantiated without the abstract methods.
claims.verified_by: Read from the same local clone.

claims.claim_vi: Python 3.13.16 programs: _balance assignable from outside; a.__secret AttributeError but a._Account__secret readable; Shape() raises TypeError; overridden step called from base run(); Duck without inheritance works; Car holds an Engine.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19.

claims.claim_vi: Timings, best of seven repeats, three runs: method call at hierarchy depth 1, 5 and 20 is 23.5-25.5 ns at every depth; 100 polymorphic calls take 3.78-3.95 us versus 7.80-8.22 us with isinstance dispatch.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19; absolute numbers belong to the test machine.

claims.claim_vi: Source states OOP has been around since the 1960s and took off in the 1990s with Java and C++, classes are blueprints for objects, and that eight key concepts exist (shown in a picture only).
